rows.stem: The next \((4^{\text{th}})\) term of the A.P. \(\sqrt{18}, \sqrt{50}, \sqrt{98}, \ldots\) is :
rows.solution:
\(\sqrt{18} = 3\sqrt{2}\), \(\sqrt{50} = 5\sqrt{2}\), \(\sqrt{98} = 7\sqrt{2}\), so the common difference is \(2\sqrt{2}\).

The next term is \(7\sqrt{2} + 2\sqrt{2} = 9\sqrt{2} = \sqrt{162}\), which is option (C) \(\sqrt{162}\).

rows.stem: If \(\dfrac{x}{3} = 2\sin A\), \(\dfrac{y}{3} = 2\cos A\), then the value of \(x^2 + y^2\) is :
rows.solution:
\(x = 6\sin A\) and \(y = 6\cos A\), so \(x^2 + y^2 = 36(\sin^2 A + \cos^2 A) = 36\).

This is option (A) \(36\).

rows.subtopic: Trigonometric Ratios of an Acute Angle
rows.stem: If \(4\sec\theta - 5 = 0\), then the value of \(\cot\theta\) is :
rows.solution:
\(4\sec\theta = 5\) gives \(\sec\theta = \dfrac{5}{4}\), so \(\cos\theta = \dfrac{4}{5}\) and \(\sin\theta = \sqrt{1 - \dfrac{16}{25}} = \dfrac{3}{5}\).

\(\cot\theta = \dfrac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta} = \dfrac{4}{3}\), which is option (D) \(\dfrac{4}{3}\).

rows.chapter: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
rows.subtopic: Consistency from the Ratios of Coefficients
rows.stem: Which out of the following type of straight lines will be represented by the system of equations \(3x + 4y = 5\) and \(6x + 8y = 7\) ?
rows.solution:
\(\dfrac{a_1}{a_2} = \dfrac{3}{6} = \dfrac{1}{2}\), \(\dfrac{b_1}{b_2} = \dfrac{4}{8} = \dfrac{1}{2}\) and \(\dfrac{c_1}{c_2} = \dfrac{5}{7}\).

\(\dfrac{a_1}{a_2} = \dfrac{b_1}{b_2} \neq \dfrac{c_1}{c_2}\), so the lines are parallel, which is option (A) Parallel.

rows.subtopic: Zeroes and Coefficients of a Quadratic Polynomial
rows.stem: The ratio of the sum and product of the roots of the quadratic equation \(5x^2 - 6x + 21 = 0\) is :
rows.solution:
For \(5x^2 - 6x + 21 = 0\), the sum of the roots is \(\dfrac{6}{5}\) and the product is \(\dfrac{21}{5}\).

Sum : product \(= 6 : 21 = 2 : 7\), which is option (B) \(2 : 7\).

rows.stem: For the data \(2, 9, x + 6, 2x + 3, 5, 10, 5\); if the mean is 7, then the value of x is :
rows.solution:
The sum of the seven observations is \(2 + 9 + (x + 6) + (2x + 3) + 5 + 10 + 5 = 40 + 3x\).

\(\dfrac{40 + 3x}{7} = 7\) gives \(40 + 3x = 49\), so \(x = 3\). This is option (D) \(3\).

rows.subtopic: Probability from a Collection of Objects
rows.stem: One ticket is drawn at random from a bag containing tickets numbered 1 to 40. The probability that the selected ticket has a number which is a multiple of 7 is :
rows.solution:
The multiples of 7 from 1 to 40 are 7, 14, 21, 28 and 35: 5 of the 40 tickets.

\(P = \dfrac{5}{40} = \dfrac{1}{8}\), which is option (B) \(\dfrac{1}{8}\).

rows.stem: The perimeter of the sector of a circle of radius 21 cm which subtends an angle of \(60^\circ\) at the centre of circle, is :
rows.solution:
Length of the arc \(= \dfrac{60}{360} \times 2 \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 21 = 22\) cm.

The perimeter of the sector is the arc plus the two radii: \(22 + 21 + 21 = 64\) cm, which is option (C) 64 cm. (22 cm is the arc alone.)

rows.stem: The length of an arc of a circle with radius 12 cm is \(10\pi\) cm. The angle subtended by the arc at the centre of the circle, is :
rows.solution:
\(\dfrac{\theta}{360^\circ} \times 2\pi \times 12 = 10\pi\), so \(\theta = \dfrac{10 \times 360^\circ}{24} = 150^\circ\).

This is option (D) \(150^\circ\).

rows.subtopic: HCF and LCM by Prime Factorisation
rows.stem: The greatest number which divides 281 and 1249, leaving remainder 5 and 7 respectively, is :
rows.solution:
The required number divides \(281 - 5 = 276\) and \(1249 - 7 = 1242\) exactly, so it is their HCF.

\(276 = 2^2 \times 3 \times 23\) and \(1242 = 2 \times 3^3 \times 23\), so HCF \(= 2 \times 3 \times 23 = 138\), which is option (C) \(138\).

rows.stem: The number of terms in the A.P. \(3, 6, 9, 12, \ldots, 111\) is :
A chord of a circle of radius 10 cm subtends a right angle at its centre. The length of the chord (in cm) is :
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - the circle with centre O, radius OA = 10 cm marked, the right angle AOB and chord AB; the stem states every value. Page idx 6.
rows.solution:
The two radii and the chord form a right triangle with the right angle at the centre, so

chord \(= \sqrt{10^2 + 10^2} = \sqrt{200} = 10\sqrt{2}\) cm, which is option (B) \(10\sqrt{2}\).

rows.subtopic: HCF and LCM by Prime Factorisation
rows.stem: The LCM of three numbers 28, 44, 132 is :
rows.solution:
\(28 = 2^2 \times 7\), \(44 = 2^2 \times 11\), \(132 = 2^2 \times 3 \times 11\).

The LCM takes the highest power of each prime: \(2^2 \times 3 \times 7 \times 11 = 924\), which is option (D) \(924\).

rows.subtopic: HCF and LCM by Prime Factorisation
rows.stem: If the product of two co-prime numbers is 553, then their HCF is :
rows.solution:
Co-prime numbers have no common factor other than 1, so their HCF is 1 whatever their product (here \(553 = 7 \times 79\)).

This is option (A) \(1\).

rows.subtopic: Zeroes and Coefficients of a Quadratic Polynomial
rows.stem: If \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) are the zeroes of the polynomial \(p(x) = kx^2 - 30x + 45k\) and \(\alpha + \beta = \alpha\beta\), then the value of k is :
rows.solution:
For \(kx^2 - 30x + 45k\): \(\alpha + \beta = \dfrac{30}{k}\) and \(\alpha\beta = \dfrac{45k}{k} = 45\).

\(\dfrac{30}{k} = 45\) gives \(k = \dfrac{30}{45} = \dfrac{2}{3}\), which is option (D) \(\dfrac{2}{3}\).

rows.subtopic: Number of Tangents from an External Point
rows.stem: In the given figure, RJ and RL are two tangents to the circle. If \(\angle RJL = 42^\circ\), then the measure of \(\angle JOL\) is :
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - that O is the centre of the circle (and OJ, OL its radii to the points of contact) is shown only in the drawing; the stem never names O. Page idx 8.
rows.solution:
Tangents from R are equal, so \(RJ = RL\) and \(\angle RLJ = \angle RJL = 42^\circ\). Then \(\angle JRL = 180^\circ - 84^\circ = 96^\circ\).

The radii OJ and OL are perpendicular to the tangents, so in the quadrilateral OJRL, \(\angle JOL = 360^\circ - 90^\circ - 90^\circ - 96^\circ = 84^\circ\).

This is option (B) \(84^\circ\).

rows.stem: In the given figure, in \(\Delta ABC\), \(DE \parallel BC\). If AD = \(2{\cdot}4\) cm, DB = 4 cm and AE = 2 cm, then the length of AC is :
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - that D lies on AB and E on AC is shown only in the drawing. Page idx 8.
rows.solution:
\(DE \parallel BC\), so by the Basic Proportionality Theorem \(\dfrac{AD}{DB} = \dfrac{AE}{EC}\): \(\dfrac{2{\cdot}4}{4} = \dfrac{2}{EC}\), so \(EC = \dfrac{8}{2{\cdot}4} = \dfrac{10}{3}\) cm.

\(AC = AE + EC = 2 + \dfrac{10}{3} = \dfrac{16}{3}\) cm, which is option (C) \(\dfrac{16}{3}\) cm.

rows.stem: If a vertical pole of length \(7{\cdot}5\) m casts a shadow 5 m long on the ground and at the same time, a tower casts a shadow 24 m long, then the height of the tower is :
rows.solution:
At the same time the sun's rays make the same angle with the ground, so the two right triangles (object, shadow, ray) are similar and height : shadow is the same for both.

\(\dfrac{h}{24} = \dfrac{7{\cdot}5}{5}\), so \(h = 1{\cdot}5 \times 24 = 36\) m, which is option (D) 36 m.

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** ABCD is a trapezium with \(DC \parallel AB\). E and F are points on AD and BC respectively, such that \(EF \parallel AB\). Then \(\dfrac{AE}{ED} = \dfrac{BF}{FC}\).

**Reason (R) :** Any line parallel to parallel sides of a trapezium divides the non-parallel sides proportionally.
rows.context: Questions number 19 and 20 are Assertion and Reason based questions. Two statements are given, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is **not** the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
A line parallel to the parallel sides of a trapezium divides the non-parallel sides proportionally (join AC; apply the Basic Proportionality Theorem in the two triangles it forms). So the Reason is true.

The Assertion is exactly this result for the line EF, so it is true, and the Reason explains it.

Both are true and the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion, which is option (A).

rows.subtopic: Geometrical Meaning of the Zeroes of a Polynomial
rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** Degree of a zero polynomial is not defined.

**Reason (R) :** Degree of a non-zero constant polynomial is 0.
rows.context: Questions number 19 and 20 are Assertion and Reason based questions. Two statements are given, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is **not** the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
The zero polynomial has no non-zero term, so no degree can be assigned to it: the Assertion is true.

A non-zero constant \(c\) can be written \(cx^0\), so its degree is 0: the Reason is true.

But the Reason is about non-zero constants and says nothing about why the zero polynomial has no degree. Both are true and the Reason is not the correct explanation, which is option (B).

rows.subtopic: Number of Tangents from an External Point
rows.stem: If two tangents inclined at an angle of \(60^\circ\) are drawn to a circle of radius 3 cm, then find the length of each tangent.
rows.solution:
Let PA and PB be the tangents from an external point P to the circle with centre O, with \(\angle APB = 60^\circ\). Join OA, OB and OP.

Triangles OAP and OBP are congruent (\(OA = OB\), \(PA = PB\), OP common), so OP bisects \(\angle APB\) and \(\angle APO = 30^\circ\). The radius OA is perpendicular to the tangent PA.

In right triangle OAP: \(\tan 30^\circ = \dfrac{OA}{AP}\), so \(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{3}{AP}\) and \(AP = 3\sqrt{3}\) cm.

Each tangent is \(3\sqrt{3}\) cm long.

rows.stem: Evaluate : \(\dfrac{2\tan 30^\circ \cdot \sec 60^\circ \cdot \tan 45^\circ}{1 - \sin^2 60^\circ}\)
rows.solution: \(\dfrac{2 \times \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \times 2 \times 1}{1 - \dfrac{3}{4}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{4}{\sqrt{3}}}{\dfrac{1}{4}} = \dfrac{16}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{16\sqrt{3}}{3}\).

rows.subtopic: Zeroes and Coefficients of a Quadratic Polynomial
rows.stem: If \(\alpha, \beta\) are zeroes of the polynomial \(p(x) = 5x^2 - 6x + 1\), then find the value of \(\alpha + \beta + \alpha\beta\).
rows.solution:
For \(5x^2 - 6x + 1\): \(\alpha + \beta = \dfrac{6}{5}\) and \(\alpha\beta = \dfrac{1}{5}\).

\(\alpha + \beta + \alpha\beta = \dfrac{6}{5} + \dfrac{1}{5} = \dfrac{7}{5}\).

rows.subtopic: Section Formula and Ratio of Division
rows.stem: Find the ratio in which the point \(P(-4, 6)\) divides the line segment joining the points \(A(-6, 10)\) and \(B(3, -8)\).
rows.solution:
Let \(P(-4, 6)\) divide AB in the ratio \(k : 1\). Then

\(-4 = \dfrac{3k - 6}{k + 1}\), so \(-4k - 4 = 3k - 6\), \(7k = 2\) and \(k = \dfrac{2}{7}\).

(Check with the ordinates: \(\dfrac{-8k + 10}{k + 1} = \dfrac{-16/7 + 70/7}{9/7} = \dfrac{54}{9} = 6\).)

The required ratio is \(2 : 7\).

rows.stem: Prove that the points \((3, 0)\), \((6, 4)\) and \((-1, 3)\) are the vertices of an isosceles triangle.

rows.subtopic: Probability from a Collection of Objects
rows.stem: A carton consists of 60 shirts of which 48 are good, 8 have major defects and 4 have minor defects. Nigam, a trader, will accept the shirts which are good but Anmol, another trader, will only reject the shirts which have major defects. One shirt is drawn at random from the carton. Find the probability that it is acceptable to Anmol.
rows.solution:
Anmol rejects only the 8 shirts with major defects, so he accepts \(60 - 8 = 52\) shirts.

\(P(\text{acceptable to Anmol}) = \dfrac{52}{60} = \dfrac{13}{15}\).

rows.subtopic: Irrational Numbers and Proof by Contradiction
rows.stem: Prove that \(\left(\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{3}\right)^2\) is an irrational number, given that \(\sqrt{6}\) is an irrational number.
rows.solution:
\(\left(\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{3}\right)^2 = 2 + 3 + 2\sqrt{6} = 5 + 2\sqrt{6}\).

Suppose, to the contrary, that \(5 + 2\sqrt{6}\) is rational. Then \(5 + 2\sqrt{6} = \dfrac{a}{b}\), where a and b are integers and \(b \neq 0\).

Rearranging, \(\sqrt{6} = \dfrac{a - 5b}{2b}\). The right side is a ratio of integers, so it is rational; but \(\sqrt{6}\) is irrational. This is a contradiction.

So the assumption is wrong, and \(\left(\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{3}\right)^2 = 5 + 2\sqrt{6}\) is irrational.

rows.subtopic: Sum of First n Terms of an AP
rows.stem: If the sum of the first 14 terms of an A.P. is 1050 and the first term is 10, then find the \(20^{\text{th}}\) term and the \(n^{\text{th}}\) term.

rows.subtopic: Sum of First n Terms of an AP
rows.stem: The first term of an A.P. is 5, the last term is 45 and the sum of all the terms is 400. Find the number of terms and the common difference of the A.P.
Prove that : \(\dfrac{\tan A}{1 - \cot A} + \dfrac{\cot A}{1 - \tan A} = 1 + \sec A \operatorname{cosec} A\)
rows.solution:
Write everything in sines and cosines:

LHS \(= \dfrac{\sin A/\cos A}{(\sin A - \cos A)/\sin A} + \dfrac{\cos A/\sin A}{(\cos A - \sin A)/\cos A}\)

\(= \dfrac{1}{\sin A - \cos A}\left[\dfrac{\sin^2 A}{\cos A} - \dfrac{\cos^2 A}{\sin A}\right] = \dfrac{1}{\sin A - \cos A} \times \dfrac{\sin^3 A - \cos^3 A}{\sin A\cos A}\)

\(= \dfrac{1}{\sin A - \cos A} \times \dfrac{(\sin A - \cos A)(\sin^2 A + \cos^2 A + \sin A\cos A)}{\sin A\cos A}\)

\(= \dfrac{1 + \sin A\cos A}{\sin A\cos A} = \dfrac{1}{\sin A\cos A} + 1 = 1 + \sec A\operatorname{cosec} A =\) RHS.

rows.subtopic: Probability with Cards, Dice and Coins
rows.stem:
Three unbiased coins are tossed simultaneously. Find the probability of getting :

(i) at least one head.

(ii) exactly one tail.

(iii) two heads and one tail.
rows.solution:
The 8 equally likely outcomes are HHH, HHT, HTH, THH, HTT, THT, TTH, TTT.

(i) Only TTT has no head, so 7 outcomes have at least one head: \(P(\text{at least one head}) = \dfrac{7}{8}\).

(ii) Exactly one tail: HHT, HTH, THH, so \(P(\text{exactly one tail}) = \dfrac{3}{8}\).

(iii) Two heads and one tail: the same three outcomes HHT, HTH, THH, so \(P(\text{two heads and one tail}) = \dfrac{3}{8}\).

rows.stem: An arc of a circle of radius 10 cm subtends a right angle at the centre of the circle. Find the area of the corresponding major sector. (Use \(\pi = 3{\cdot}14\))
rows.solution:
Area of the circle \(= 3{\cdot}14 \times 10 \times 10 = 314\ \text{cm}^2\).

Area of the minor sector (angle \(90^\circ\)) \(= \dfrac{90}{360} \times 314 = 78{\cdot}5\ \text{cm}^2\).

Area of the major sector \(= 314 - 78{\cdot}5 = 235{\cdot}5\ \text{cm}^2\).

rows.subtopic: Nature of Roots and the Discriminant
rows.stem: Find the value of ‘k’ for which the quadratic equation \((k + 1)x^2 - 6(k + 1)x + 3(k + 9) = 0\), \(k \neq -1\) has real and equal roots.

rows.subtopic: Solving a Quadratic Equation by Factorisation
rows.stem: The age of a man is twice the square of the age of his son. Eight years hence, the age of the man will be 4 years more than three times the age of his son. Find their present ages.
rows.solution:
Let the son's present age be x years. Then the man's present age is \(2x^2\) years.

Eight years hence: \(2x^2 + 8 = 3(x + 8) + 4\), so \(2x^2 - 3x - 20 = 0\).

\(2x^2 - 8x + 5x - 20 = 2x(x - 4) + 5(x - 4) = (2x + 5)(x - 4) = 0\), so \(x = 4\) or \(x = -\dfrac{5}{2}\). An age cannot be negative, so \(x = 4\).

The son is 4 years old and the man is \(2 \times 4^2 = 32\) years old. (Check: in 8 years they will be 40 and 12, and \(3 \times 12 + 4 = 40\).)

rows.stem: From a point on a bridge across the river, the angles of depressions of the banks on opposite sides of the river are \(30^\circ\) and \(60^\circ\) respectively. If the bridge is at a height of 4 m from the banks, find the width of the river.
rows.solution:
Let P be the point on the bridge and PQ = 4 m its height above the line of the banks, with the banks at A and B on opposite sides of Q. The angles of depression equal the angles of elevation at the banks: \(\angle PAQ = 30^\circ\) and \(\angle PBQ = 60^\circ\).

In right triangle PAQ: \(\tan 30^\circ = \dfrac{PQ}{AQ}\), so \(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{4}{AQ}\) and \(AQ = 4\sqrt{3}\) m.

In right triangle PBQ: \(\tan 60^\circ = \dfrac{PQ}{QB}\), so \(\sqrt{3} = \dfrac{4}{QB}\) and \(QB = \dfrac{4}{\sqrt{3}}\) m.

Width of the river \(= AQ + QB = 4\sqrt{3} + \dfrac{4}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{12 + 4}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{16}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{16\sqrt{3}}{3}\) m \(\approx 9{\cdot}24\) m.

rows.stem: In the given figure, \(\Delta FEC \cong \Delta GDB\) and \(\angle 1 = \angle 2\). Prove that \(\Delta ADE \sim \Delta ABC\).
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the configuration is defined only by the drawing: D on AB and E on AC, F and G on BC produced beyond B and C, the lines FE and GD crossing, and the angles 1, 2 (at D and E in triangle ADE) and 3, 4 (at B and C) marked. Page idx 16.
rows.solution:
In the figure, \(\angle 1 = \angle ADE\), \(\angle 2 = \angle AED\), \(\angle 3 = \angle ABC\) and \(\angle 4 = \angle ACB\).

\(\Delta FEC \cong \Delta GDB\), so their corresponding angles at C and B are equal: \(\angle ECF = \angle DBG\). Since CE lies along CA and CF along CB, and BD lies along BA and BG along BC, this says \(\angle 4 = \angle 3\).

In triangle ABC, \(\angle 3 = \angle 4\), so \(AB = AC\) ... (i)

In triangle ADE, \(\angle 1 = \angle 2\), so \(AD = AE\) ... (ii)

Dividing (ii) by (i): \(\dfrac{AD}{AB} = \dfrac{AE}{AC}\). By the converse of the Basic Proportionality Theorem, \(DE \parallel BC\).

So \(\angle 1 = \angle 3\) and \(\angle 2 = \angle 4\) (corresponding angles), and by the AA criterion \(\Delta ADE \sim \Delta ABC\).

rows.stem: Sides AB and AC and median AD of a \(\Delta ABC\) are respectively proportional to sides PQ and PR and median PM of another \(\Delta PQR\). Show that \(\Delta ABC \sim \Delta PQR\).
rows.solution:
Given: \(\dfrac{AB}{PQ} = \dfrac{AC}{PR} = \dfrac{AD}{PM}\), where AD and PM are medians. To prove: \(\Delta ABC \sim \Delta PQR\).

Construction: produce AD to E so that \(DE = AD\), and join EC. Produce PM to L so that \(ML = PM\), and join LR.

Proof: in triangles ABD and ECD, \(BD = DC\) (AD is a median), \(AD = DE\) and \(\angle ADB = \angle EDC\) (vertically opposite). So \(\Delta ABD \cong \Delta ECD\) (SAS), giving \(AB = EC\) and \(\angle BAD = \angle CED\). In the same way \(PQ = LR\) and \(\angle QPM = \angle RLM\).

Now \(\dfrac{EC}{LR} = \dfrac{AB}{PQ} = \dfrac{AC}{PR} = \dfrac{AD}{PM} = \dfrac{2AD}{2PM} = \dfrac{AE}{PL}\).

So \(\Delta AEC \sim \Delta PLR\) (SSS similarity), and their corresponding angles are equal: \(\angle CAE = \angle RPL\) and \(\angle AEC = \angle PLR\).

From \(\angle AEC = \angle PLR\): \(\angle BAD = \angle CED = \angle PLR = \angle QPM\).

Adding, \(\angle BAD + \angle CAD = \angle QPM + \angle RPM\), that is \(\angle BAC = \angle QPR\).

With \(\dfrac{AB}{PQ} = \dfrac{AC}{PR}\) and the included angles equal, \(\Delta ABC \sim \Delta PQR\) (SAS similarity).

rows.subtopic: Surface Area of a Combination of Solids
rows.stem: A wooden article was made by scooping out a hemisphere from each end of a solid cylinder, as shown in the figure. If the height of the cylinder is \(5{\cdot}8\) cm and its base is of radius \(2{\cdot}1\) cm, find the total surface area of the article.
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - a cylinder with a hemisphere scooped out of each end; every value is in the stem. The page render (idx 18) shows the image tiled above a black block; the marking scheme reprints it cleanly (ms idx 14). Page idx 18.
rows.solution:
The article's surface is the curved surface of the cylinder together with the inner curved surfaces of the two scooped-out hemispheres (the flat ends are gone). Here \(r = 2{\cdot}1\) cm and \(h = 5{\cdot}8\) cm.

Curved surface area of the cylinder \(= 2\pi rh = 2 \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 2{\cdot}1 \times 5{\cdot}8 = 76{\cdot}56\ \text{cm}^2\).

Curved surface area of the two hemispheres \(= 2 \times 2\pi r^2 = 4 \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 2{\cdot}1 \times 2{\cdot}1 = 55{\cdot}44\ \text{cm}^2\).

Total surface area of the article \(= 76{\cdot}56 + 55{\cdot}44 = 132\ \text{cm}^2\).

rows.chapter: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
rows.stem: If the number of children visited be x and the number of adults visited be y, then write the given situation algebraically.
rows.context:
Essel World is one of India’s largest amusement parks that offers a diverse range of thrilling rides, water attractions and entertainment options for visitors of all ages. The park is known for its iconic “Water Kingdom” section, making it a popular destination for family outings and fun-filled adventure. The ticket charges for the park are ₹ 150 per child and ₹ 250 per adult.

On a day, the cashier of the park found that 300 tickets were sold and an amount of ₹ 55,000 was collected.

Based on the above, answer the following questions :
rows.figureNote: DECORATIVE - a photograph of a roller coaster; every number is in the passage. Page idx 18.
rows.solution:
300 tickets were sold: \(x + y = 300\).

₹ 55,000 was collected at ₹ 150 a child and ₹ 250 an adult: \(150x + 250y = 55000\), that is \(3x + 5y = 1100\).

rows.chapter: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
rows.stem: How many children visited the amusement park that day ?
rows.context:
Essel World is one of India’s largest amusement parks that offers a diverse range of thrilling rides, water attractions and entertainment options for visitors of all ages. The park is known for its iconic “Water Kingdom” section, making it a popular destination for family outings and fun-filled adventure. The ticket charges for the park are ₹ 150 per child and ₹ 250 per adult.

On a day, the cashier of the park found that 300 tickets were sold and an amount of ₹ 55,000 was collected.

Based on the above, answer the following questions :
rows.solution:
The tickets give \(x + y = 300\) and the money \(150x + 250y = 55000\), that is \(3x + 5y = 1100\).

From the first, \(y = 300 - x\). Substituting: \(3x + 1500 - 5x = 1100\), so \(2x = 400\) and \(x = 200\).

200 children visited the park that day.

rows.chapter: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
rows.stem: How many adults visited the amusement park that day ?
rows.context:
Essel World is one of India’s largest amusement parks that offers a diverse range of thrilling rides, water attractions and entertainment options for visitors of all ages. The park is known for its iconic “Water Kingdom” section, making it a popular destination for family outings and fun-filled adventure. The ticket charges for the park are ₹ 150 per child and ₹ 250 per adult.

On a day, the cashier of the park found that 300 tickets were sold and an amount of ₹ 55,000 was collected.

Based on the above, answer the following questions :
rows.solution:
The tickets give \(x + y = 300\) and the money \(150x + 250y = 55000\), that is \(3x + 5y = 1100\).

Multiply the first by 3 and subtract: \(2y = 1100 - 900 = 200\), so \(y = 100\).

100 adults visited the park that day.

rows.chapter: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
rows.stem: How much amount will be collected if 250 children and 100 adults visit the amusement park ?
rows.context:
Essel World is one of India’s largest amusement parks that offers a diverse range of thrilling rides, water attractions and entertainment options for visitors of all ages. The park is known for its iconic “Water Kingdom” section, making it a popular destination for family outings and fun-filled adventure. The ticket charges for the park are ₹ 150 per child and ₹ 250 per adult.

On a day, the cashier of the park found that 300 tickets were sold and an amount of ₹ 55,000 was collected.

Based on the above, answer the following questions :
rows.solution:
At ₹ 150 a child and ₹ 250 an adult, the amount \(= 250 \times 150 + 100 \times 250 = 37500 + 25000 = 62500\).

₹ 62,500 will be collected.

rows.stem: Find the coordinates of the point which divides the line segment joining points P and R in the ratio \(2 : 1\) internally.
rows.context:
A garden is in the shape of a square. The gardener grew saplings of Ashoka tree on the boundary of the garden at the distance of 1 m from each other. He wants to decorate the garden with rose plants. He chose a triangular region inside the garden to grow rose plants. In the above situation, the gardener took help from the students of class 10. They made a chart for it which looks like the given figure.

Based on the above, answer the following questions :
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the coordinates of P and R exist only in the grid drawing. Page idx 20.
rows.solution:
With \(P(4, 6)\) and \(R(6, 5)\) read from the grid, the point dividing PR internally in the ratio \(2 : 1\) is

\(\left(\dfrac{2 \times 6 + 1 \times 4}{3}, \dfrac{2 \times 5 + 1 \times 6}{3}\right) = \left(\dfrac{16}{3}, \dfrac{16}{3}\right)\).

rows.stem: Find out if \(\Delta PQR\) is an isosceles triangle.
rows.context:
A garden is in the shape of a square. The gardener grew saplings of Ashoka tree on the boundary of the garden at the distance of 1 m from each other. He wants to decorate the garden with rose plants. He chose a triangular region inside the garden to grow rose plants. In the above situation, the gardener took help from the students of class 10. They made a chart for it which looks like the given figure.

Based on the above, answer the following questions :
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the coordinates of P, Q and R exist only in the grid drawing. Page idx 20.
rows.solution:
With \(P(4, 6)\), \(Q(3, 2)\) and \(R(6, 5)\): \(PQ = \sqrt{1 + 16} = \sqrt{17}\), \(QR = \sqrt{9 + 9} = \sqrt{18}\) and \(PR = \sqrt{(6 - 4)^2 + (5 - 6)^2} = \sqrt{5}\).

No two sides are equal, so triangle PQR is not isosceles.

rows.stem: What is the median class of the above given data ?
rows.context:
Activities like running or cycling reduce stress and the risk of mental disorders like depression. Running helps build endurance. Children develop stronger bones and muscles and are less prone to gain weight. The physical education teacher of a school has decided to conduct an inter school running tournament in his school premises. The time taken by a group of students to run 100 m, was noted as follows :

| Time (in seconds) | 0 – 20 | 20 – 40 | 40 – 60 | 60 – 80 | 80 – 100 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Number of students | 8 | 10 | 13 | 6 | 3 |

Based on the above, answer the following questions :
rows.figureNote: DECORATIVE - an overhead photograph of sprinters on a running track; the data are in the table. Page idx 22.
rows.solution:
| Time (in seconds) | 0-20 | 20-40 | 40-60 | 60-80 | 80-100 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Number of students (f) | 8 | 10 | 13 | 6 | 3 |
| cf | 8 | 18 | 31 | 37 | 40 |

\(N = 40\) and \(\dfrac{N}{2} = 20\). The first cumulative frequency above 20 is 31, so the median class is 40-60.

rows.stem: Find the mode of the above given data.
rows.context:
Activities like running or cycling reduce stress and the risk of mental disorders like depression. Running helps build endurance. Children develop stronger bones and muscles and are less prone to gain weight. The physical education teacher of a school has decided to conduct an inter school running tournament in his school premises. The time taken by a group of students to run 100 m, was noted as follows :

| Time (in seconds) | 0 – 20 | 20 – 40 | 40 – 60 | 60 – 80 | 80 – 100 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Number of students | 8 | 10 | 13 | 6 | 3 |

Based on the above, answer the following questions :
rows.solution:
The highest frequency is 13, so the modal class is 40-60, with \(l = 40\), \(f_1 = 13\), \(f_0 = 10\), \(f_2 = 6\), \(h = 20\).

Mode \(= l + \dfrac{f_1 - f_0}{2f_1 - f_0 - f_2} \times h = 40 + \dfrac{13 - 10}{26 - 10 - 6} \times 20 = 40 + \dfrac{3}{10} \times 20 = 46\) seconds.
